card.name: Rash stop rule and visual inspection
card.fires_on: Two stock phrases in drug labels: 'rash' in 'discontinue at the first sign of rash', and 'inspected' in 'parenteral drug products should be inspected visually'.

modes.label: First sign of rash
modes.description: The word rash right after an instruction to discontinue the drug at the first sign of it.
modes.example: discontinue armodafinil tablets at the first sign of<< rash>>, unless the rash is clearly not drug

modes.label: Inspect injectables visually
modes.description: The word inspected (or a similar verb) in the standard sentence about checking parenteral products for particles and discoloration.
modes.example: Parenteral drug products should be<< inspected>> visually for particulate matter and discolor

card.writes: It pushes toward the word safety and risk terms, which suggests it adds a safety-instruction framing.
card.plain: It lights up on fixed label sentences telling you to stop at the first sign of rash or to visually check injectable solutions.
